messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-89321 fired -> lb-targets-unhealthy (eu-west-2). Automatically opened in #incidents. Symptoms: TLS handshake failures from edge to backend + 502/504 spike. Auto-annotated: region=eu-west-2 severity=high

pagerduty: PD-89321 acknowledged by @oncall-alex (oncall)

oncall-alex: i'm on it, stepping in. seeing alerts in console, routing/health dashboards loading slowly. starting by checking ALB target group health and recent deploys

sre_ian: looking at prometheus: 5xx rate jumped ~18% for eu-west-2 at 7054321080. Backend TLS handshake errors correlate with increased connection resets. grafana -> edge->backend TLS handshake_fail metric spiked

eng-mari: any recent canary rollouts? i don't see a CI job in last 30m but can check deploy logs. also curious if cert rotation was happening in that region

netops-zoe: quick dns check: Route53 hosted zone shows records for edge-load.eu with TTL=60. ran dig from multiple pts:
```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
edge-load.eu. 60 IN A 10.2.3.45
edge-load.eu. 60 IN A 10.2.3.46
```
some nodes still resolving to older ip (~10.2.3.44) at certain vantage points. could be propagation + cached routes

oncall-alex: curl from eu probe -> backend returns: `curl: (35) SSL: Handshake failed`
```
$ curl -v https://10.2.3.45/health
* Connected to 10.2.3.45 (10.2.3.45) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake: SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
```

sre_ian: running openssl s_client against ip shows mismatched certificate CN (svc.internal) vs expected edge cert; TLS handshake failing when client enforces SNI. Looks like some backends are serving the wrong cert (maybe leftover from canary host)

eng-mari: checked rolling deploy logs — a canary of a config change (sni-bypass flag) was applied 12m ago to target subset 10.2.3.45-46, and a scripted cert reload ran. rollback not automatic. that matches timing. i'm seeing increased RSTs in backend logs for 10.2.3.45

netops-zoe: ALB target group health shows ~40% unhealthy on tg-eu-1. Targets flapping between healthy/unhealthy.

oncall-alex: mitigation idea: remove problematic targets from ALB target group to stop hitting misconfigured canary, shift traffic to fallback pool. executing runbook failover now: `/ops/failover.sh --tg tg-eu-1 --remove 10.2.3.45`

eng-mari: ack. i'll also trigger a graceful restart of the backend service on remaining targets and roll back the canary config to ensure certs are consistent.

pagerduty: PD-89321 escalated to L2 after 8m: notifying eng-mari

eng-mari: taking ownership of remediation. running rollback: `kubectl -n prod set env deployment/backend SNI_BYPASS=false --record` then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/backend`

support-liz: heads up — external monitoring and some customer requests showing ~18% error rate for EU customers since the spike. ticket volume is low but steadily increasing. putting message in status page draft

oncall-alex: removed 10.2.3.45 from tg-eu-1 and set draining. immediate drop in 5xx rate on the ALB within 30s. monitoring for regressions

sre_ian: after removal, global error rate down to baseline in eu nodes that hit fallback pool. still seeing isolated TLS fails from edge nodes that resolved to stale IPs (10.2.3.44)

netops-zoe: digging DNS path — some edge nodes had cached A record with low TTL but stuck due to intermediate resolver misbehavior. opening ticket with provider, but as short-term we can widen fallback by lowering weight on region canaries and increase health check frequency

eng-mari: rollout rollback completed; backend certs reloaded and verified. `openssl s_client -connect 10.2.3.46:443 -servername edge.example.com` shows correct CN and successful handshake

pagerduty: PD-89321: update posted. status: mitigated. oncall acknowledged by eng-mari

support-liz: posting incident note to status.redwood.ai: partial outage for EU customers impacting 15-20% of requests. advise customers to retry; no data loss reported.

oncall-alex: handing over to eng-mari for postmortem and root cause analysis. my shift ends in 17m. tagging @eng-mari and @netops-zoe for RCA and follow-ups

eng-mari: will own RCA. initial hypothesis: canary config + cert reload introduced inconsistent certs on subset of hosts; combined with DNS propagation/edge caching meant some edge nodes continued to hit stale/unhealthy instances -> TLS handshake failures + 5xx spikes.

netops-zoe: immediate action items:
- increase ALB healthcheck frequency for tg-eu-1 to 10s for next 2h
- temporarily lower canary weight to 0 across region until validated
- request resolver vendor to flush caches for problematic prefixes

eng-mari: engineering action items:
- add sanity check in deploy pipeline that validates cert CN and TLS handshake post-reload
- make canary rollback automatic if TLS handshake failure rate > 1% within 5m
- add a dashboard for cert reload vs TLS handshake failure correlation

support-liz: customer comms: drafted message, will send after eng confirmation that mitigation succeeded.

oncall-alex: closing in-channel page: PD-89321 resolved at 7054322840. leaving incident thread for RCA and postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PD-89321 closed by @eng-mari. Incident duration ~29m.

eng-mari: will publish a concise postmortem within 48h with timeline, root cause, and automated guardrails planned. adding netops-zoe and support-liz as owners for their action items.

support-liz: filing customer impact summary and list of affected customers (anonymized) to the incident doc.

sre_ian: adding logs and graphs to the incident doc; will include raw openssl outputs and ALB health snapshots.

netops-zoe: created vendor ticket #VND-1347 for resolver cache flush and asked for ETA

eng-mari: thx team. once RCA draft is ready i'll ping #postmortems for review.
